sections.en:
1 megasti v : megasiti M : megastr P : megaster L : menasin G. almagest P.
2 Minor perfectus ('Minor perfect') L v : Maior profectus ('Major advance') G M. Bonum dominus ('Good lord') (hand 2: domini ('of the lord')) M :
Domini fuit scienti ('It was of the lord to the knowing') L. Bonum dominus fuit scire vel sic ('The good lord was to know or thus') : Bonum quidem fecerunt ('Indeed they did good')
illi ('those'). De eodem ('Concerning the same') M. vv. 2-4 (quod autem ('but that')) I have supplied from codices G M. The rest have
tantum ('only') : Quod tamen in eo ('Which however in it'). 4 Mesahalath M. 5 Quod autem in Almagesti et in ('But that in the Almagest and in')
commento Gebri prolixe ('the commentary of Geber at length') M. 6 restrictum est ('is restricted') G : distinguitur ('is distinguished') L. Azerbeel P :
Arzabel G : Azarchele L v (badly, see below concerning Azarchel p. 90, n. 2) : Attraleey M:
alibi ('elsewhere') Algazele (Steinschneider). 7 Albategni et incipit ('Albategni and begins') L. 8 Inter ('Between') omitted by v. 9 ex sus- ('from sus-')
pectione ('picion') L. radicis ('of the root') M : radicum ('of the roots') G L P : cuiusdam ('of a certain') v. Abrachoz P : Abrachas G :
Abruchis L. 10 quae tamen ('which however') omitted by G. contra fidem pugnare ('to fight against faith') v : fide pugnare ('to fight with faith') M :
fidem pungere ('to puncture faith') P L : contra fidem pungere ('to puncture against faith') G. librum ('book') omitted by L. 11 secundum ('according to')
Euclidem ('Euclid') L : stilum Euclidis ('the style of Euclid') G : Oiclidis P : Euclidis M.

sections.text:
1 Versio Syntaxis mathematicae quam Gerardus de Cremona saec. XII confecit,
incipit verbis : Bonum fuit, scire [pro Syre], quod sapientibus. Cf. Steinschneider,
Zum speculum, p. 381, § 40 a.
2 Geber est Djabir ben Aflah Hispanus († circa 1150); cf. Suter, Mathematiker
und Astronomen der Araber, p. 119, n° 284. Eius astronomia a Gerardo Cremo-
nensi latine versa et anno 1534 Norimbergae edita est.
3 De Messahala vel rectius Mashallah, qui temporibus chalifarum Almansoris
et Almamunis floruit, vide Catal. I, p. 81, n. 1, et indicem huius libri. Cf. Suter,
Mathemat. und Astronomen der Araber, 1900, p. 5, n° 8. — Liber ab Alberto Magno
laudatus editus est Norimbergae a. 1504, iterum a. 1549; cf. Steinschneider, Zum
speculum, p. 376 n° 37 a.
4 Azerbeel corruptus esse videtur. Albategnius est celeberrimus astronomus
Muhamed-ben-Djabir Al-Battâni († 929 p. C.). Cf. Suter, op. cit., p. 45, n° 89. —
Opus eius a Platone Tiburtino translatum est et Norimbergae a. 1537 prodiit.
Praefatio Platonis incipit : Inter universa liberalium artium ; cf. Steinschneider,
Zum speculum, p. 539, n° 5.
5 Abrachus vel Abrachis est Hipparchus; cf. Steinschneider, Zum speculum,
p. 359. Albertus praefationem Platonis Tiburtini transcribit ubi legitur : (Albate-
gnius) qui Ptolemaei prolixitatem compendiose coartat, eiusque errores emendans,
qui quidem rarissimi sunt, non ipsi sed Abrachis radici imputat.
sections.en:
1 The version of the Mathematical Syntaxis which Gerard of Cremona made in the 12th century,
begins with the words: It was good, to know [for Syre], what to the wise. Cf. Steinschneider,
Zum speculum, p. 381, § 40 a.
2 Geber is Djabir ben Aflah the Spaniard († circa 1150); cf. Suter, Mathematiker
und Astronomen der Araber, p. 119, no. 284. His astronomy was translated into Latin by Gerard of Cremo-
na and published in Nuremberg in the year 1534.
3 On Messahala or more correctly Mashallah, who flourished in the times of the caliphs Almansor
and Almamun, see Catal. I, p. 81, n. 1, and the index of this book. Cf. Suter,
Mathemat. und Astronomen der Araber, 1900, p. 5, no. 8. — The book praised by Albert the Great
was published in Nuremberg in the year 1504, again in the year 1549; cf. Steinschneider, Zum
speculum, p. 376 no. 37 a.
4 Azerbeel seems to be corrupt. Albategnius is the most famous astronomer
Muhamed-ben-Djabir Al-Battâni († 929 A.D.). Cf. Suter, op. cit., p. 45, no. 89. —
His work was translated by Plato of Tivoli and appeared in Nuremberg in the year 1537.
The preface of Plato begins: Among all the liberal arts; cf. Steinschneider,
Zum speculum, p. 539, no. 5.
5 Abrachus or Abrachis is Hipparchus; cf. Steinschneider, Zum speculum,
p. 359. Albert transcribes the preface of Plato of Tivoli where it is read: (Albate-
gnius) who compendiously shortens the prolixity of Ptolemy, and correcting his errors,
which indeed are very rare, imputes them not to him but to the root of Abrachis.

summary.headline: Almagest and Its Commentators
summary.text: Discussion of the Almagest or Mathematical Syntaxis under the titles Megasti, Almagesti, and Maior perfectus, comparing treatments by Geber, Messahalah, and Albategni. It describes the motion of the orb, Albategni’s corrections to Ptolemy attributed to Abrachis, and a subsequent compilation in the style of Euclid containing both Ptolemy’s and Albategni’s opinions.
